_meta.indication: For the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) or anti-muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) antibody positive.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study; randomization 1:1:1 stratified by presence of anti-AChR or anti-MuSK autoantibodies.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with generalized myasthenia gravis who are anti-AChR or anti-MuSK antibody positive and with MGFA Class II to IVa.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to day 43 in the MG-ADL score after the 6-week treatment cycle.
pivotal_trials.n: N=200 randomized (placebo n=67; rozanolixizumab ~7 mg/kg n=66; ~10 mg/kg n=67).
pivotal_trials.result: Difference in LS mean change from baseline in MG-ADL score vs placebo was -2.59 (95% CI: -4.09, -1.25; p<0.001) for the ~7 mg/kg dose and -2.62 (95% CI: -3.99, -1.16; p<0.001) for the ~10 mg/kg dose, in favor of rozanolixizumab.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) were headache (44% vs 19% placebo), infections/any infection (23% vs 19%), diarrhea (20% vs 13%), pyrexia (17% vs 2%), hypersensitivity reactions (11% vs 5%), and nausea (10% vs 8%). Serious risks include infections and aseptic meningitis.
target_moa: Rozanolixizumab is a neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) blocker; it decreases serum IgG concentration, including anti-AChR- and anti-MuSK-specific pathogenic IgG, by inhibiting the binding of IgG to FcRn, leading to enhanced degradation of IgG.
modality: mAb (recombinant, humanized anti-FcRn IgG4P monoclonal antibody).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened (Advisory Committee Summary: Not applicable).

orphan_indication.text: Rozanolixizumab was granted orphan drug designation on February 1, 2019, for the treatment of gMG.
